reasons: Compliant classification is supportable on the cited text: Section 14 (p0079) conditions continued service on 'Client provides ... written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement' with no requirement of cause, breach, consent or justification, i.e. a functional Customer convenience exit with an effective ~30-60 day tail, and no early-termination fee, penalty or clawback appears anywhere in the fee or term provisions (p0045, p0078).

Vendor side is acceptable: TrueLink's only mid-term exits in p0078 are for-cause (System/Credit Repository Agreement default or Client breach of Sections 8a-8c), so there is no Vendor convenience right during the committed term.

Walk-away test is not engaged: the initial term is 1 year with successive one-year renewals, so the 'no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term' trigger and the detection guidance's >12-month threshold do not apply.

Correct output form for a compliant finding: no redline (rendered text is byte-identical to the original) and no counterparty comment, consistent with the instruction that a clause meeting preferred or fallback is not reopened.

The failed deterministic check is properly treated as a phrasing variant, not cured by an edit. Inserting 'for convenience' into p0079 would redline a clause that already meets the position and would needlessly reopen our best exit right; the check should be waived by the reviewer.

Noted rather than flagged, correctly: the mutual 30-day non-renewal notice in p0078 is shorter than the fallback's 90 days for a Vendor end-of-term exit, but it is symmetrical non-renewal (equally available to us) rather than a mid-term convenience right, and is more naturally addressed under an auto-renewal/notice rule than double-flagged here.

Minor: the rationale carries process narration about repeated check failures and unrelated cleanup items (Section 13 cross-reference, blank Section 4 commitment). These are legitimate internal notes but should be trimmed to the substantive compliance analysis before the finding is filed as evaluation evidence.
